findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, oversized file)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and propagate fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| ...)

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is hidden I/O side effect inside a data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: functional core leaks imperative shell concerns; callers cannot suppress logging; pure tests see spurious stdout
findings.fix: remove println! entirely from core logic; logging belongs in the imperative shell at the call site

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked indexing into a Vec with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: empty lines, lines with a single comma-less field, or malformed CSV panics with index out of bounds at runtime
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1) with ok_or_else to return a typed ParseError for malformed lines

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap on parse failure and lossy cast via as u16
findings.failure_mode: non-numeric or out-of-range input in the value field panics; values >65535 silently truncate via as u16
findings.fix: use get(1) with ok_or_else, then u32::from_str with map_err, then u16::try_from(value) with map_err to return a typed ParseError

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy width cast that silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value like 70000 becomes 4416 in the Record, corrupting data with no error signal
findings.fix: replace `as u16` with `u16::try_from(parsed_u32)?` or `try_into().map_err(...)` to fail on overflow

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string, println!) with data parsing in a single public function with no Result return type
findings.failure_mode: function signature `-> Vec<Record>` cannot express any failure; callers have no way to handle errors; functional core contract is violated
findings.fix: change signature to `pub fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>` and move all I/O into a shell-level adapter

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec<String> for a two-field record; SKILL.md mandates split_once for first-delimiter extraction
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line, worse performance, and more memory pressure on large files
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get (name_part, value_part) without collecting; trim each part individually

findings.problem: .map(|part| part.trim().to_string()) creates intermediate String allocations for every field
findings.failure_mode: excess heap allocations per line; with split_once you can keep &str throughout the parsing pipeline
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and work with &str slices; only allocate the final Record String fields

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist to measure load_sessions throughput, allocation count, or memory profile
findings.failure_mode: performance claim is unsubstantiated; allocation-heavy implementation has no measured baseline
findings.fix: add criterion or similar benchmarks measuring lines-per-second, allocations-per-line, and peak memory for representative file sizes

findings.problem: No try_reserve on the Vec before collecting; no checked capacity arithmetic for expected line count
findings.failure_mode: repeated reallocations as Vec grows; if line count is known or bounded, unbounded growth is wasteful and allocation failure is unhandled
findings.fix: compute expected capacity with checked_mul/checked_add, call results.try_reserve(capacity)? before the iterator chain, and remove Vec::with_capacity

findings.problem: No test modules or test files exist for this crate
findings.failure_mode: no behavior contract exists; regression coverage is zero; all invariants are unproven by automated means
findings.fix: add tests covering: valid two-field CSV, empty lines, single-field lines, non-numeric value fields, values exceeding u16 max, missing file, and permission denied

findings.problem: value is a bare u16 with no domain constraint; any u16 value is accepted including meaningless ones
findings.failure_mode: illegal values are representable; domain invariants are not enforced at the type level
findings.fix: wrap u16 in a newtype `SessionValue(u16)` with a fallible constructor that validates domain constraints

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for stated performance claims
no profiler data (criterion, perf, or flamegraph) for load_sessions throughput or allocation profile
no allocation tracking (tracing, dhat-rs, or cargo-bench with --bench-args) for bounded allocation handling
no behavior tests exist for any function in this crate
no command evidence (cargo test, cargo clippy) was executed; static review only
residual_risk: Multiple BLOCKER violations: unwrap on I/O and parse (panic on untrusted input), unchecked indexing (panic on malformed lines), lossy as cast (silent data corruption), hidden println! I/O in functional core, split+collect instead of split_once, no Result return type, no try_reserve, no allocation checks. The function as written will panic on any malformed input, missing file, or values outside u16 range. All unsafe constructs must be eliminated and the function must return Result with typed errors before this code is safe for any use.
